How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very complicated and demanding

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to submit all materials to Yonsei in late April. This included my TOEFL score, transcript, bank statement, etc. I received a response in late May, after which I had to apply for a dorm, upload insurance documentation, and register for courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I emailed my home university and my host university

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Also very complicated. First of all, the website Yonsei provides with course options is very confusing. Second, the registration process only started a week before the semester began, and after that, I had to apply for pre-approval from my home university to ensure that I was actually allowed to take the selected courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It complicated and time demanding, but worth it. Contact former students who have been on exchange to the same country/university

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Very mixed. In general, my impression was that the courses exclusively for exchange students were generally easier than the courses that were for both exchange students and local students.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In general, a very different structure. I am used to lectures where you listen to a professor. At Yonsei, it was much more classroom-based teaching, where attendance, participation, etc., were important.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It is indeed a different culture, but it was quite and fast to adjust to the local culture

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Choose courses were there also are local students and not only exchange students

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
The language was a bit of a challenge since some places only have signs in Korean, and many people do not speak English. However, Google Translate (with the image function) was very helpful.

Additionally, there are some cultural norms, such as staying quiet on public transportation, showing respect for elders, receiving and giving things with both hands, etc.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The safety and public transportation (good)

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Bring two credit cards (revolut worked very well)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The Korean government will send a bill for their National Health Insurance. However, you can get an exemption and avoid paying it if you already have a travel/health insurance.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the people you meet, truly understanding and getting to know a culture, personal development, improvements in English.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The most challenging part was living in a dorm in a very small room with another person.
